title: NBC Sports, U.S. Ski & Snowboard, FIS revamp media rights deal
article_text:
NBC Sports has revamped its media rights deal with U.S. Ski and Snowboard and the International Ski Federation (FIS), a move that will allow it to air every alpine World Cup and World Championship race this season.

FIS did not use an agency on the rights talks with NBC.

NBC and U.S. Ski & Snowboard extended their deal through 2030.

NBC will air alpine events on Peacock, offering additional coverage on NBC and NBCSN for major events. All domestic events will additionally be available on Peacock and YouTube.

“For years, fans had to work harder than they should have to watch our athletes compete,” U.S. Ski and Snowboard President Sophie Goldschmidt said. “We are thrilled that the new centralized broadcast strategy we’ve worked on with FIS and the other countries removes that friction. This is a new era, which now makes it easier to watch our sports and follow your favorite athletes.”

NBC’s current deal for the U.S. rights to the Olympics runs through 2036.

Its coverage of the 2026-27 season kicks of Saturday with men’s and women’s giant slalom races in Sölden, Austria. Those will air live on Peacock and on NBC Sports Network on Sunday evening.

U.S. Ski and Snowboard and FIS also have created a YouTube and FAST channel under the same name, Ski & Snowboard World Cup, that will include all World Cup and World Championship events in cross country, freeride, freeski, freestyle, nordic combined, ski jumping and snowboard.

C15 Studio will distribute and operate the FAST channel.

title: World Rugby hires event exec Rose to lead first US World Cup
article_text:
The World Rugby governing body has appointed Megan Rose as managing director of the 2031 men’s Rugby World Cup as preparations ramp up for the first-ever edition in the US.

In the role, she will lead delivery planning for what is described as the “biggest and most ambitious” Rugby World Cup.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

A former professional tennis player, Rose is an experienced major event executive in US sport, with a track record of delivering high-profile global competitions.

During a stint at the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Rose led major events including the US Open Series, Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup, and served as team leader for Team USA Olympic Tennis at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.

Rose said: "Rugby World Cup is one of the iconic events in global sport, defined by unforgettable moments on the pitch and the passion of fans around the world. To be entrusted with bringing the men’s Rugby World Cup to the United States for the first time is an extraordinary honour, and I’m thrilled to join this team.

“This tournament represents a once-in-a-generation opportunity to bring millions more Americans into the game and create a lasting impact for rugby in this country. I look forward to working closely with USA Rugby, and the clubs, players, supporters, and stakeholders who have built rugby across the United States, alongside the global rugby community, to deliver an incredible Rugby World Cup and build something that lasts well beyond 2031.”

The appointment comes as momentum continues to build behind the USA hosting programme, with 25 cities currently progressing through the Rugby World Cup 2031 applicant phase.

The US will also stage the 2033 Women’s Rugby World Cup. World Rugby stated that holding its flagship events in the market is central to the organization’s “strategic ambition to grow participation, audiences, and commercial revenues by unlocking rugby’s full potential in sport’s biggest global market.”

Alan Gilpin, World Rugby chief executive, added: "The USA represents one of the most exciting growth opportunities in global sport, and Rugby World Cups 2031 and 2033 have the potential to transform rugby’s profile and reach on an unprecedented scale.

“Megan is an outstanding leader with a proven track record of delivering world-class sporting events and driving innovation. She joins us at a pivotal moment as our U.S. project enters its next phase –an appointment that reflects the scale of our ambition.

“Her experience, vision, and deep understanding of the U.S. sports landscape make her ideally placed to deliver a defining chapter for rugby in the United States and around the world.”

Meanwhile, World Rugby is continuing to build out the commercial program for the 2027 men’s Rugby World Cup and the next women’s edition in 2029, with supermarket retailer Woolworths brought in as the latest partner.

Woolworths will serve as the official supermarket supporter of the tournaments, both taking place in Australia.

The agreement grants the company integrated commercial rights across both marquee tournaments, with the store to roll out fan-focused activations, promotions, and community health initiatives.

The partnership also incorporates Woolworths Group’s retail media business, Cartology, enabling supplier brands and FMCG advertisers to run targeted retail media campaigns across digital, in-store, and point-of-sale channels throughout the tournament cycles.

The deal expands Woolworths’ sports sponsorship portfolio, which includes tie-ups with Cricket Australia, Netball Australia, Netball New Zealand, the Australian Olympic Committee, and Paralympics Australia.

Last month, credit card giant Visa was unveiled as a commercial partner of the 2027 and 2029 World Cups, while soft drinks giant Coca-Cola was also recently signed up for the upcoming men's event.

The sponsorship portfolio for the 2027 men’s tournament also includes top-tier principal partners Emirates Airlines and Japanese beverage company Asahi, as well as Dove Men+Care, Gilbert, Macron, LipovitanD, Mitsubishi Estate, Meiji, Fanatics, Ticketmaster, and ChildFund Rugby, who all serve as third-tier suppliers and supporters.

The tournament, which features an expanded 24-team, 52-match format across six weeks in seven Australian host cities, will take place next year between October 1 and November 13.

title: Publicis goes full throttle on sport with acquisition of 160over90
article_text:
It’s a surprise that Publicis Groupe hasn’t gone all-out on sports marketing already, but CEO Arthur Sadoun is attempting to put that right with the acquisition of 160over90, just in time for the start of the FIFA World Cup in June. The global sports and entertainment agency was previously part of WME Group, owner of well-known talent agency William Morris Endeavor.

160over90 brings on board more than 670 employees in the US, UK, EMEA and APAC in a deal thought to be worth around $600 million. Publicis claims that 160over90’s offering will plug in neatly to the agency group’s existing data and creator capabilities, helping the French group to take advantage of the $150 billion sports media market, plus $90 billion of sponsorship opportunities.

Publicis Sport launched in October 2025 with Suzy Deering, formerly of Verizon, Ford and eBay, as its CEO – presumably with this acquisition in mind.

Sadoun said: “In the age of AI, sport has become one of the most high-value channels for clients… By combining 160over90’s scale and expertise in sports experiences, culture, and talent with the industry’s most powerful connected influencer platform, experiential capabilities, and data-driven insights, we are disrupting a highly fragmented landscape by creating a unified, end-to-end platform that connects brands to fans in ways that are both meaningful and measurable.”

Mark Shapiro, president and managing partner of WME Group,said: “Combining forces with Publicis Sports will create an unmatched offering for brands looking to move faster and create deeper connections with sports fans, properties, and content. Additionally, WME Group’s new collaboration with Publicis Groupe will deliver more opportunities for our talent and partners to realize their business ambitions at scale”

title: European Athletics Champs return to Helsinki, Torun gets indoor event
article_text:
Finland’s capital Helsinki has been awarded hosting rights for the 2030 European Athletics Championships.

Helsinki was one of two bidders for the biennial multi-sport event, along with Brussels.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The decision was taken at the 181st European Athletics Council Meeting in Lausanne, Switzerland, today.

This will be the fourth time the European Athletics Championships will be held in the Finnish capital after previous editions in 1971, 1994 and 2012, making Helsinki the most prolific host city for the championships.

The 2030 edition will be held in the city's Olympic Stadium, which reopened in 2020 after extensive renovation.

As well as three previous iterations of the European Athletics Championships, Helsinki hosted the 1952 Olympic Games along with the 1983 and 2005 editions of the World Athletics Championships, becoming the first city to stage the championships twice.

European Athletics CEO Christian Milz said: “Finnish athletics fans are among the most passionate and knowledgeable in Europe and the consistently exceptionally strong television audiences for the European Athletics Championships in Finland demonstrates just how deeply our sport resonates with the Finnish public.

“Indeed, the 2026 European Athletics Championships yielded an average market share of 74% across the week, and television audiences peaked at 1.3 million for Alisa Vainio’s victory in the women’s marathon on the final day of the championships.

“We are certain the championships will generate huge interest not only locally but across the rest of Europe and beyond.”

Earlier this year, European Athletics announced that the next edition of its flagship event will be staged in the Polish city of Silesia from 3 to 8 June 2028.

This will be the first time that the European Athletics Championships will be held on Polish soil in the event's 92-year history.

This year’s European Athletics Championships were held in Birmingham, UK, from August 10 to 16. The 2024 edition was staged in Rome.

Finland won two gold medals in Birmingham courtesy of Silja Kosonen and Vainio in the women’s hammer and women’s marathon, respectively.

Riikka Pakarinen, president of the Finnish Athletics Federation, said: “This was a fantastic conclusion to a three-year bid project and the starting gun for the operational work to create a memorable event at the Helsinki Olympic Stadium for both athletes and spectators.

“Hopefully this will also encourage other Finnish sports to bid for major international events in Finland. We have a world-class stadium, ready infrastructure, a strong athletics heritage and growing public interest. With Finnish athletics still enjoying a strong upswing, the conditions for successful European Championships are in place.”

Meanwhile, at the council meeting in Lausanne, the 2029 European Athletics Indoor Championships were also awarded to Torun, Poland.

This will be the second time Torun has hosted the biennial championships this decade, having also staged the 2021 edition despite the severe restrictions caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

The city also hosted the 2026 World Athletics Indoor Championships.

The 2029 European Athletics Indoor Championships will take place in the Kujawsko-Pomorska Arena in Torun.

The 2027 edition of the event will be held in Valencia, Spain, from March 4 to 7.

title: Sheehan switches to number eight for Munster derby
article_text:

title: Fresh questions now raised over Etihad Stadium naming rights deal after £750,000 revelation
article_text:
Manchester City's Etihad Stadium naming rights agreement has come under renewed scrutiny after a Freedom of Information disclosure revealed the council's share of the deal was capped at £750,000 per year.

The revelation has prompted fresh questions over the value Manchester City Council received from the arrangement, with the stadium lease now under review.

According to The i Paper, the Cityzens agreed to pay Manchester City Council 50% of naming rights revenue, subject to an annual cap of £750,000, when the stadium lease was renegotiated in October 2010.

The agreement came months before Etihad Airways signed a major sponsorship package in 2011 covering the stadium, club shirts and surrounding campus.

The ten-year deal was reported at the time to be worth around £400m, with the stadium naming rights portion estimated at between £10m and £15m annually. Neither party publicly confirmed the precise figures.

The stadium was originally built using public and lottery funding for the 2002 Commonwealth Games, costing £112m. Although Manchester City Council retains ownership, the club operates the venue under a 250-year lease.

The disclosure has raised concerns about whether the council secured sufficient value for a public asset. The issue comes amid wider scrutiny of City's commercial agreements.

An independent commission found that sponsorship arrangements involving Etihad and other partners included payments from the club's Abu Dhabi owners that artificially inflated revenue. City recorded £86.75m in sponsorship fees in 2011-12, of which £16m was described as base fees paid by sponsors, with the remaining £70.75m topped up by Abu Dhabi United Group.

Manchester City Council has confirmed that the stadium lease is under review, with the club's £300m expansion nearing completion.

The £750k cap highlights why transparency matters when public assets are used in commercial agreements with private football clubs.

The council's share should be assessed against the full terms of the lease, the risks it carried and the benefits the wider development brought to Manchester.

With the stadium lease under review, the authorities have an opportunity to explain how the arrangement was structured and whether it remains appropriate following the expansion.

“We all know that all sports federations face challenges in continuing as Olympic sports, and one of the challenges facing the Fencing Federation is the lack of sufficient financial support. Previously, we had the elected President, Alisher Usmanov [RUS], who donated approximately ten million Swiss francs annually, and this is where the development of fencing began.

“After the President’s decision to suspend his activities due to personal circumstances, it became difficult for the International Fencing Federation to continue its development, while other Federations increased their budgets and proceeded with their development plans. I won’t hide the fact that the Fencing Federation has been operating for more than three years simply to survive, without any development, with a very low budget, and we currently have no sponsors.

“We need a development plan that guarantees our continued competitiveness with other Federations to maintain our position as an Olympic sport. This plan requires at least twenty-five million, a number we arrived at after numerous studies, because it is difficult for us to secure this amount at the moment. This was the minimum amount we determined.

“We are starting the development process, and reaching the level of development we desire will require no less than fifteen million, of which seven and a half million are already secured.”

That’s International Fencing Federation Interim President Abdel Moneim El Husseiny (EGY), speaking at the November 2025 FIE Congress concerning the federation’s finances, with Russia’s Usmanov elected to a fifth term in 2024, but recusing himself immediately due to continuing sanctions against him from the European Union. From 2008 to 2021, he donated more than CHF 87 million or about $100 million U.S., but nothing after the Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. El Husseiny stated that Usmanov was living in Bahrain at the time of the 2025 Congress.

Asked about the CHF 7.5 million he mentioned, El Husseiny explained.

“[W]e know exactly the names, but we cannot announce now the names because it’s confidential until we can sign the contract and it will be launched for all of you. So, for privacy reasons, I cannot say now the name, but I give you a clue that it’s … two of them are from Gulf area, and one of them will be from Asia. You can wait maybe one more month because we’ll start at the beginning of 2026, and you will all know at that time the names of these sponsors.”

The 2026 FIE Congress is coming up on 21-22 November in Budapest (HUN), and the federation has posted its financial report for 2025. Its Web site currently shows two sponsors: Kazakhstan-based Integra Construction and fencing equipment supplier Absolute Fencing, headquartered in Bridgewater Township, New Jersey; no mention of sponsors from Gulf countries. There are also 40 more suppliers listed, mostly involved in the fencing trade, from multiple countries.

“Regarding revenue, the most significant income came from the [International Olympic Committee], specifically from the Olympic Games, totalling 12,766,306 Swiss francs. This represents 85% of our revenue. We also had 11% of revenue from financial products, investments, and financial equivalents, amounting to 1,651,376 Swiss francs.” (CHF 1 = $1.23 U.S. in November 2025.)

For 2025, the audited statements showed the federation is still in a difficult situation (CHF 1 = $1.21 U.S. today):

● CHF 2.763 million operating income (68% from IOC)

● CHF 7.891 million operating expenses (3% below budget)

● CHF 6.972 million total loss after financial losses

Assets at the end of 2025 were down from CHF 32.058 million at the end of 2024 and reserves of CHF 30.946 million. Thanks to the IOC’s television rights fee payment, the FIE showed a surplus of CHF 8.951 million in 2024.

There’s no report on 2026 so far, but the 2027 budget showed a presumed CHF 7.5 million in sponsorship for the second straight year, with total revenue expected at CHF 15.555 million. The FIE budget plan shows:

● 2026 budget for revenue & expense: CHF 14.260 million (balanced)

● 2027 budget for revenue & expense: CHF 15.550 million (balanced)

Administrative costs are projected for 2027 at CHF 2.85 million or 18.3% of the total.

The FIE’s situation is stable for now, thanks to its very careful spending and its reserves. But it leaped from spending CHF 6.82 million in 2025 to a planned CHF 14.26 million in 2026. Unless the sponsorship efforts bear fruit, that kind of increased spending is not sustainable for long.

I am currently serving as President with full authority, there is no interference in my work, and I am overseeing things as a former Olympic fencer. I love fencing and I respect it. title: Why Stripe is Sponsoring F1’s Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS Team
article_text:
Programmable financial services company Stripe has announced a multiyear global partnership with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1.

Stripe will collaborate across the team’s global commercial operations, applying its technology to support the evolution of its financial capabilities as the team’s Official Global Payments Partner and an Official Team Partner.

Its technology will run across Mercedes’ global commercial operations.

- Finance firms make up 74% of finance and crypto sponsors on the 2026 grid.

Stripe has grown largely through developers adopting its products rather than through brand advertising: the Mercedes deal therefore marks a notable change in how the company markets itself.

It is one of two major sports deals for Stripe in 2026, with the company also becoming a worldwide partner of the Ryder Cup in July.

Stripe’s branding will appear on the team’s cars and assets from the first race of the 2027 season, but before then, the first of a series of product deployments will launch at key races in the rest of 2026, beginning with the team’s retail experience.

John Collison, Co-Founder and President at Stripe, says: “Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team has built one of the most ambitious and successful organisations in sports.

“Behind that is an extraordinary standard of engineering and a relentless drive to improve. That combination resonates with how we build at Stripe.

“We’re looking forward to applying that same approach to the financial infrastructure supporting their next stage of growth.”

For Mercedes, the partnership is about modernising the financial infrastructure behind a commercial business. That business spans merchandise, fan experiences and partner relationships.

Toto Wolff, Team Principal and CEO of the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team, says: “When the opportunity arose to rethink our approach in this sector, we wanted to be ambitious and partner with the very best.

“Stripe was the only choice. Having a partner that has Stripe’s expertise and their huge reach will help us build the right foundations for the future as we continue to develop our business in this fast-moving and increasingly connected world.”

Chief Commercial Officer for the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team, Richard Sanders, says the complexity of running a business across a global will create a more cohesive experience for fans, partners and stakeholders.

“As part of such a global sport, we operate across multiple markets, currencies and customer touchpoints, from merchandise and experiences to partner relationships and international transactions.

“Stripe’s platform will help us simplify and strengthen the way we manage those interactions.”

- Shopify has run Shopify Payments on Stripe’s infrastructure since the service launched in 2013. The relationship has since expanded beyond card processing, with Stripe Treasury powering Shopify Balance, the platform’s business account for merchants. That makes Shopify one of Stripe’s largest platform partners.

- Amazon uses Stripe to process payments across several of its businesses, including Prime and Audible, under a partnership the two companies expanded in 2023. The relationship runs both ways, as Stripe is also a long-standing customer of Amazon Web Services (AWS).

- OpenAI uses Stripe to handle payments for ChatGPT subscriptions. In September 2025, the two companies launched Instant Checkout in ChatGPT and co-developed the Agentic Commerce Protocol, an open standard that lets AI agents complete purchases directly on a user’s behalf.

title: Former Scotland Rugby International Tim Visser to Stand Trial on Rape and Abuse Charges
article_text:
Former Scotland rugby international Tim Visser is set to stand trial after being accused of rape and abusive behaviour towards a woman.

The 39-year-old faces four charges relating to alleged incidents between 2010 and 2024.

Two charges allege that Visser raped the woman on various occasions.

He also faces allegations of threatening, controlling and abusive behaviour.

The charges include claims of physical violence and controlling aspects of the woman's daily life.

His defence lawyer, Ian Duguid, entered a plea of not guilty on his behalf.

A trial has been scheduled to begin in Edinburgh on 12 January 2028.

Born in the Netherlands, Visser chose to represent Scotland at international level.

The winger made 33 appearances for Scotland between 2012 and 2017.

He also played club rugby for Newcastle Falcons, Edinburgh and Harlequins before retiring in 2019.

The allegations have not been proven in court, and Visser denies the charges.

title: Karolina Muchova secures final qualification place for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells
article_text:
The WTA on Wednesday announced Karolina Muchova has qualified for the FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells to confirm the star-studded singles field and set tennis' ultimate stage for the world's best athletes.

Muchova is the eighth and final singles qualifier for the preeminent championships in women's sport, joining PIF WTA World No.1 Elena Rybakina, Indian Wells and Miami champion Aryna Sabalenka, Roland-Garros winner Mirra Andreeva, Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, American superstars Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula along with trailblazing mother Elina Svitolina at Indian Wells.

"Earning a place at the FAGE WTA Finals is an extraordinary achievement, and I can't wait to welcome our eight singles players to Indian Wells," WTA Finals Tournament Director Garbiñe Muguruza said. "This is the ultimate stage, where the best play the best. With its passionate fans and stunning desert backdrop, the Indian Wells Tennis Garden will be a fantastic setting to crown our champions."

Muchova, who is from the Czech Republic, has qualified for the WTA Finals for the second time after withdrawing from the 2023 event because of an injury.

The doubles teams of Hsieh Su-Wei & Jelena Ostapenko and Ellen Perez & Demi Schuurs also confirmed their qualification for the FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells following impressive seasons on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz.

Karolina Muchova has enjoyed success this year at every level of the WTA Tour and across all three surfaces, winning titles on hard court at the WTA 1000 Qatar TotalEnergies Open (Doha) and on grass at the WTA 500 Bad Homburg Open powered by Solarwatt.

She reached an additional final on clay, finishing runner-up at the WTA 500 Porsche Tennis Grand Prix and also contested her second Grand Slam final at The Championships, Wimbledon.

Hsieh Su-Wei and Jelena Ostapenko will be making their second appearance as a team at the WTA Finals and enjoyed a run to the semifinals last year. Overall this will be Hsieh Su-Wei's seventh appearance, winning the title in 2013 and also finishing as runner-up three times, while this will be Ostapenko's fourth outing, having also qualified once for the WTA Finals in singles in 2017.

The pairing have reached two finals this year, kicking off 2026 by winning the WTA 500 Brisbane International and contesting the title match at the WTA 1000 Qatar TotalEnergies Open in Doha.

This season marks Ellen Perez and Demi Schuurs' first qualification as a team though both bring extensive WTA Finals experience, with Schuurs having reached three semifinals and Perez reaching the title match in 2023.

The duo have shown great consistency this season, contesting the final at the WTA 500 Bad Homburg Open powered by Solarwatt, reaching two semifinals at the Adelaide International and Porsche Tennis Grand Prix in Stuttgart (both WTA 500 events) and a further eight quarterfinals across 2026.

Hsieh Su-Wei & Ostapenko and Perez & Schuurs' qualification leaves one final doubles place remaining.

The WTA Finals Indian Wells features the Top 8 singles and doubles teams on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard (with the 8th spot going to the singles player and doubles team that have won a Grand Slam if ranked No.8 to No.20). This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. title: Warren Gatland issues denial, confirms English offer and shares big family news
article_text:
Warren Gatland has denied he applied for the Fiji head coach role, despite reports in the country that he was desperately close to getting the job.

Reports in Fiji claimed that Gatland was one of the favoured candidates, alongside the man eventually hired - former Springbok boss Jake White. As well as the reports in Fiji, sources close to the appointment process said that Gatland was believed to have applied.

The speculation grew so intense that Fijian players had reportedly been informed he was getting the job.

However, that was short-lived, with White getting the job just a day after those reports.

And the former Wales coach has now distanced himself from the official application process, saying he only held talks with Fiji's governing body.

"I did speak to them and then I just said, look, I'm not going to follow through with applying for the job," Gatland told Boyle Sports, who offer rugby odds.

"I mean look, they're an exciting team. I think Jake White will do a good job with them. You feel like with a team like that there's a lot of things you can do to improve on, but yeah, it's just the timing wasn't quite right.

"I had a grandson born a couple of weeks ago now, a third grandchild, and we had just settled. If something else came along and I felt it was the right thing, I would look at something."

Gatland had previously been linked with Gallagher Prem club Harlequins earlier this year, as a director of rugby at the Stoop.

However, that didn't materialise amid reports that Gatland wasn't keen to take on the bulk of the coaching.

"I did speak to Harlequins during the year," added Gatland. "They made me an offer, but the timing wasn't quite right.

"It's a club that I've always had a bit of time for - they've got a pool of players to develop from in terms of youngsters.

"That would have been potentially exciting, but just the timing wasn't quite right for me.

"Maybe a club role [would appeal] or something like that. International rugby is really tough because I don't think people appreciate the limited preparation time.

"You've got basically five or six training sessions, you're playing an international, and people expect you to win.

"The good thing about club stuff is that you've almost got an opportunity to experiment and fail to succeed.

"You can try things and it doesn't quite work out. You don't have that luxury in international rugby."

Gatland has not held a permanent role since leaving the Wales coaching job for the second time midway through the 2025 Six Nations, after overseeing 14 consecutive defeats - eventually being replaced by Steve Tandy.

title: Three ex-All Blacks and Sevens star named in Samoa's Nations Cup squad
article_text:
Head coach Tusi Pisi has handed a handful of All Blacks places in his 30-man Manu Samoa squad for the November leg of the World Rugby Nations Cup, with fixtures against Zimbabwe, Portugal and Spain on the horizon.

The headline inclusions are former All Blacks Akira Ioane, Josh Ioane and Shaun Stevenson, who are among eight uncapped players selected for the campaign.

All three qualify for Samoa through heritage and were cleared by World Rugby’s eligibility regulations earlier this year, opening the door to an international switch after previously representing New Zealand.

The trio are joined by another high-profile uncapped addition in Etene Nanai-Seturo.

The former New Zealand Sevens star and All Blacks XV representative has long been viewed as a player with Test rugby potential and will be hoping to cement a place in Samoa’s plans ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Under World Rugby’s eligibility rules, players can switch unions after a stand-down period provided they have a qualifying birthright connection to their new nation. None of Ioane, Ioane, Stevenson or Nanai-Seturo have represented New Zealand within the last three years.

Up front, Samoa’s squad boasts considerable experience. Former Wallabies loosehead Scott Sio and Munster tighthead Michael Alaalatoa headline a seasoned front row group, while Saracens’ Theo McFarland returns as one of the key figures in the second row.

The squad also includes uncapped scrum-half Efeso Tuivaiti, prop Millenium Sanerivi, lock Samuel Slade and back-rowers Lamandado Mustuga and Abraham Papali’i among the newcomers pushing for a first Test cap.

title: Exeter bring in forward Goedhals from South Africa
article_text:

title: The state of the game: key takeaways from IFR’s inaugural report on English football
article_text:
The State of the Game (SotG) report published on 13th October 2026 is the IFR’s first major output. The 245-page report sets out the regulator’s assessment of the financial health of the game and provides an early indication of how interventionist it may be in applying its licensing powers. As a draft publication, the IFR must consider any responses before issuing its final report by May 2027.

The report sets out the IFR’s view that English football is in poor financial health at all levels of the game. It considers that a new package of financial support is needed to sustain the football pyramid. This must be accompanied by action that will reduce financial risk, but changes should not undermine the success of the game.

Growth: Football, particularly the Premier League, has been excellent at driving revenue growth, with huge amounts of inward investment. The UK£9 billion of revenue in English football in 2025/2026 is far higher than any comparable market.

Lack of cost control: Despite strong revenue growth, an inability to control wages means 94 per cent of clubs are loss making and under severe financial pressure. This is because clubs continue to spend heavily on players to improve on and off-field performance and grow their enterprise value.

Financial cliff edges: One contributor to wage inflation is the cliff edges between divisions, where a promotion leads to a big jump in prize money, broadcasting, and commercial revenue. This incentivises overspending and excessive risk taking, as clubs chase the financial rewards on offer from progression through the leagues. Equally, relegation can be catastrophic to a club’s long -term financial health, as revenue drops sharply.

title: Poppi’s latest sports deal puts it ‘on the sidelines of culture’—literally
article_text:
Whether it’s the Super Bowl or the NBA Finals, Poppi has been involved in some of the biggest moments on the sports calendar.

Even so, “I would not say we’re trying to become a traditional sports marketer,” Kristina MacIntosh, the brand’s SVP of marketing, said.

Poppi’s sport marketing approach is more about becoming part of the conversations happening on the sidelines, in the stands, and on social media than it is about the on-field action, MacIntosh said. That’s why the brand’s new sponsorship of the Dallas Cowboys started not with the team’s players, but with its cheerleaders.

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders—and their massive social reach—are the centerpiece of the sponsorship, which also includes more traditional elements, MacIntosh said. The deal includes in-stadium, retail, and social content with the team and cheerleaders, as well as pouring rights at AT&T Stadium, in-stadium and retail branding, and opportunities for ticket and merch giveaways throughout the season.

The strategy offers a look at how Poppi is carving out a unique space in the evolving world of sports sponsorship, amid stiff competition in the soft-drink category.

“We really sit within those sidelines of culture, and that’s been a strategy for us since day one,” MacIntosh told us. “We want to make sure that it makes sense for the brand to connect with highly engaged communities and participate in the moments that people are caring about and talking about on their feed…We’re looking for those opportunities where sports and culture really connect.”

Poppi’s deal with the Cowboys is partially rooted in both organizations’ ties to Dallas, Texas, where Poppi was founded, but the brands have more in common than the Lone Star State.

Both “have grown into brands that have that cultural relevance beyond just their standard category,” MacIntosh said.

Becoming an official sponsor of the team also offers Poppi a “strong creative opportunity” to integrate into the world of the Cowboys, she noted, as well as multiple touchpoints to activate the partnership. The cheerleaders have served as the “way in” to more football content for the brand, MacIntosh said. To announce the partnership, a Reel on the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ page showed four of the athletes using Poppi cans as hair rollers.

This isn’t Poppi’s first rodeo. The brand has advertised in the Super Bowl, was the official soda of Inter Miami last season, and has an active, multiyear deal with the Los Angeles Lakers. The Lakers’ sponsorship has resulted in increased awareness in LA, MacIntosh told us, and the Poppi team also got in on this year’s New York Knicks hype train: During the NBA Finals, when entrepreneur and influencer Jordyn Woods-Towns (who is married to Knicks star Karl-Anthony Towns) went viral for her orange bag, Poppi sent her an orange can to pose with on Instagram.

While “zillennial girlies” tend to be Poppi’s core audience, according to MacIntosh, her team doesn’t want to alienate any potential consumers, which is why their sports partnerships are designed with wide reach in mind, combining team deals with related influencer content. Awareness and trial are also KPIs for the Cowboys partnership, which will ideally be driven by pouring rights, MacIntosh said.

MacIntosh declined to share any details about any potential Super Bowl plans, but she said she’s thinking a lot about big TV sports moments of a different variety: fictional sports properties, most notably in the romance genre.

Marketing Brew informs marketing pros of the latest on brand strategy, social media, and ad tech via our weekday newsletter, virtual events, marketing conferences, and digital guides.

After the explosion of shows including Heated Rivalry and Off Campus, MacIntosh said she’s eager to identify that “next BookTok moment” and capitalize on it, whether that be with an official content partnership or influencer work.

“How do we lean into things that are happening on and off the screen?” she said. “We’re seeing [sports] evolve to entertainment from a multifaceted approach, which is a really fun place to play.”

title: George Hendy: Northampton Saints back out to fight way into England side
article_text:
Northampton back George Hendy says he is determined to force his way into England contention, with next month's Nations Championship matches fast approaching.

Hendy has been one of the Saints' form players over the past few seasons, making match-winning contributions in the Prem final victories in 2024 and 2026.

But while a host of club-mates have become regulars for their country, the 24-year-old has had to bide his time.

"I just want to throw my hat in the ring for England and I'm really quite serious about that," Hendy told BBC Sport.

"Whether that's on the wing or at 15, whatever gives me the best opportunity to get into that squad, I want to take it, and I am pretty happy with the direction I am going in."

England boss Steve Borthwick will name a training squad on Sunday in preparation for the November leg of the Nations Championship.

Borthwick's side recovered from a chastening Six Nations to win two of their three summer matches, and now welcome Australia, Japan and New Zealand to London before the finals weekend at the end of the month.

A genuine talent with the ball in hand, Hendy says he has been working hard at all parts of his game after conversations with the England management.

"I've known for a while what my work-ons are and it feels like the penny's finally dropping," he added.

"I think my USP is being able to beat defenders and being able to finish tries. And just because I'm working on other things doesn't mean I stop working on that, so I know that if I keep doing that stuff ball in hand whilst touching up the other aspects of my game I'll be in a pretty good spot.

"I've had a few [conversations with the England coaches]. Myself and the Saints coaches know exactly what I need to do to kick on to that next level and all I can do is do that on the weekends."

Hendy says he is inspired by the example of his Northampton team-mates, with Fin Smith, Tommy Freeman, Alex Coles, Alex Mitchell, Henry Pollock and Fraser Dingwall among those to become England stalwarts.

"That makes me want it even more, I think, seeing your mates going and putting on an England shirt and doing what they love doing and representing their country," Hendy said.

"And then you get to see them and you're hearing all about the stories. I just want to be a part of that as well.

"I know that with them in camp, it'll be a good environment. I'll know who I can rely on. I work well with Fin and Tommy Freeman and Mitch.

"All those things, I think, can strengthen my opportunity if I get the chance, so that is what I am going for.

"My motivation is I just don't want to die wondering. I want to at least go into camp and experience it and if I do crack under the pressure of camp then I know that I've still got work to do.

"But it's one of those where you don't know until you get given the opportunity whether you can or you can't.

"So I'm just going to keep putting my best foot forward here and if international call-ups happen they happen and if not, I know I'm not doing a good enough job."

title: Former New England Patriots NFL star completes rugby switch
article_text:

title: Emirates Match Official appointments confirmed for World Rugby Nations Cup 2026 climax in November
article_text:

title: Seven Scotland hopefuls behind Gregor Townsend's delayed squad announcement
article_text:
Gregor Townsend has taken the anomalous decision to delay announcing his Scotland squad by one week ahead of the Nations Championship.

Originally scheduled to be released on Tuesday 20 October, Townsend has pushed back the decision until next Monday with the purpose of allowing this weekend’s fixtures to be played.

The dual benefit rationale is to monitor the fitness levels of several players poised to return from injury – or recently back – and to allow others to stake a final claim to be included.

It’s unquestionably the logical decision and there’s extreme competition for several places in the squad ahead of a monumental year of rugby.

The newly formed Nations Championship provides a third competitive tournament for Scotland to compete in, alongside the Six Nations and the World Cup next October.

Townsend has built a squad with strong cohesion and he will realistically want to work with a similar group of players as the tournaments increase in importance, culminating in the World Cup in Australia.

A hugely encouraging opening three games in the Nations Championship this summer has Scotland strongly positioned heading into the triple-header against New Zealand, Australia and Japan.

The significance of the Nations Championship splits opinion. To many, they are glorified friendlies; to others, they are important tests, but it’s irrefutable that they are perfect preparation for Scotland’s upcoming challenges in the Six Nations and World Cup.

With Townsend delaying his squad to run the rule over contenders to be called up, we’ve analysed seven players with their hopes firmly in the balance.

Ritchie has yet to feature since joining Glasgow Warriors from Perpignan due to ankle and Achilles issues, but he’s expected to debut against Benetton this weekend.

Glasgow have been extremely cautious with Ritchie’s rehabilitation and he could realistically have featured sooner. If the former Scotland international comes through the trip to Italy unscathed, then it would be a surprise if he’s not included by Townsend.

Scotland are well-stocked at back-row, particularly with the emergence of Edinburgh duo Freddy Douglas and Liam McConnell, but Ritchie’s leadership and breakdown skills are still invaluable.

His inclusion will hinge on whether Townsend believes one game is enough for Ritchie to prove his fitness, but he could also be released for Glasgow’s fixture against the Lions to improve his match-sharpness.

A few years ago, it would have been incomprehensible to envisage Duhan van der Merwe’s place in the Scotland squad being in jeopardy, even when fit.

Van der Merwe and Darcy Graham are Scotland’s two leading try scorers and were nailed-on starters for many years, but that’s all changed. Kyle Steyn and Jamie Dobie have usurped the Edinburgh duo to become first-choice options and Duhan’s place in the squad will depend on him proving his fitness against the Lions on Friday.

Van der Merwe hasn’t played this season but he’s available after recovering from foot and ankle injuries. It remains firmly in the balance, however, whether Van der Merwe will even get called up even if he shows no ill-signs on Friday. Moreover, he won’t realistically feature against New Zealand or Australia.

If Jones is fit then he should be in the squad but he’s no longer a guaranteed starter. Rory Hutchison deserves to keep the 13 jersey after an excellent summer and his role in a rampant Northampton side, while Stafford McDowall was preferred at Glasgow last season. Jones has been a phenomenal performer for Scotland over the years and justifiably earned a place in World Rugby Men’s Dream Team of the Year in 2025.

The 32-year-old was outstanding for the British & Irish Lions but he’s played limited minutes since then. Jones hasn’t been at his best since moving to Toulon and missed their win over Edinburgh last weekend due to concussion.

There’s not been much detail provided, but Jones should return against Pau and be included by Townsend, although the Scotland head coach will want to observe him.

Gilchrist has admitted himself that he needs to convince Townsend to include him with a strong performance against the Lions on Friday night. The 36-year-old returned from a biceps injury from the bench against Toulon but it’s more difficult for older players to rediscover their optimum level after injury.

Gilchrist has been an absolute stalwart for Scotland and he’s hugely admired by Townsend but some would argue it’s time to look to the future. The Edinburgh man will be 37 by next October and while he’s determined to match Chris Paterson’s record of four World Cups, there can’t be any room for sentiment in sport. There are numerous exciting young locks emerging and the question for Townsend will be whether he values Gilchrist’s experience over their superior physicality and athleticism.

There was more uncertainty around Kinghorn’s inclusion earlier in the week – when this article was originally scheduled for publication – due to injury. The 29-year-old hasn’t played for Toulouse since suffering muscular issues against Vannes in mid-September, on his first start of the season.

That firmly left Kinghorn’s place in the Scotland squad in the balance but it’s understood that he’ll play this weekend against Perpignan. Kinghorn is one of the players Townsend wanted to wait on and he should be named in the squad, provided there are no issues this weekend.

Naturally, Kinghorn will be lacking match sharpness should he be included and there’s legitimate debate around his starting role against New Zealand with Kyle Rowe impressing at full-back in the summer.

Leylah Fernandez says if she ever speaks to Emma Raducanu about their US Open final, ‘it’s really strange’
article_text:
Leylah Fernandez and Emma Raducanu made history when they reached the US Open final in 2021.

Fernandez and Raducanu were part of the first all-teenage women's singles final at the US Open in 22 years at the 2001 New York major.

This was a huge breakthrough for both players, as Raducanu beat Fernandez to become the first ever player in history to win a Grand Slam title as a qualifier.

As a result of this final, there has been a lot of attention on both Raducanu and Fernandez's careers since then, and now the latter has given an insight into their relationship.

Fernandez was asked about the US Open final against Raducanu in a newly released interview with German outlet Tennis Magazin, which took place earlier this year.

While Fernandez admitted that she has never spoken to Raducanu about the final before, she hopes to do so at some point when both of their careers are over.

"It's really strange, but we've never talked about it," said Fernandez. "Probably because of our mentality: we're competitors, we're still playing against each other.

"But I think we'll catch up on it when our careers are over. That we can sit down for coffee and say, "Remember when we managed that?" Then we can share funny stories about it. Right now, we're still so young and have many years ahead of us on the tour. We'd rather look ahead."

Fernandez played Raducanu in the biggest match of her career so far, but they have not faced each other in the five years since then.

Fernandez and Raducanu have had very different trajectories since the 2021 US Open, mostly as a result of physical issues to the latter.

Raducanu has the higher career-high ranking of the two players, having been world number 10 in 2022, but Fernandez is the much higher-ranked player of the two right now as the world number 30.

Fernandez has won five of her six WTA titles since the 2021 US Open final, most recently at the WTA 500 tournament in Singapore. However, Raducanu is yet to get her hands on any silverware since then, having reached her first two finals since winning the US Open at the Transylvania Open and the Queen's Club Championships this year.

In terms of Grand Slam tournaments, it is Fernandez who has got the closest to reaching another final, having made it to the quarter-finals of Roland Garros in 2022. Raducanu's best run at a major was at her home major of Wimbledon in 2024, when she reached the fourth round.

A significant feature of Fernandez's run to the US Open final in 2021 was her three wins against top 10 players, but she has not found as much success against the best players since then, with Raducanu struggling even more in this category.

Fernandez still has two more tournaments to play in 2026, while Raducanu appears to have ended her season already after not playing since her aforementioned run to the Queen's final, when she suffered a stress fracture in her lower right foot.

While they have not played against each other since the 2021 US Open final, there will be a lot of attention if Raducanu does ever play Fernandez again.

title: ATP Safe Sport prevents 234,000 abusive comments reaching players & fans
article_text:
ATP Safe Sport prevented more than 234,000 abusive comments from reaching players and fans across ATP and player social media channels during the past year, helping protect the tennis community from online abuse.

Delivered in partnership with Tennis Data Innovations (TDI), sports technology company Sportradar, Social Protect and Arwen AI, ATP Safe Sport was launched in 2024 as part of the ATP's broader commitment to player welfare. Combining AI-enabled moderation, specialist threat assessment, investigations and collaboration with law enforcement authorities, the programme continues to evolve and strengthen its ability to protect players from online harm.

During its second year, ATP Safe Sport analysed more than 3.7 million comments across ATP and player social media channels. More than 284,000 abusive comments were identified, with over 82% removed in real time before reaching players and fans.

The findings highlight the scale of the challenge facing professional tennis players online. More than 85 per cent of players who received social media engagement were subjected to abusive comments originating from more than 100,000 social media accounts.

As online abuse continues to grow across sport, ATP Safe Sport has expanded both its reach and capability to better support players. Following the introduction of Social Protect, moderation services are now available to men’s tennis players across all ATP rankings, alongside enhanced platform coverage, automated threat alerts and a dedicated mobile application.

Beyond content moderation, the programme continued to strengthen its safeguarding capabilities. More than 1,800 comments were escalated for specialist assessment, alongside 690 automated threat alerts. Every alert was reviewed by trained investigators to assess potential risks to players and determine whether further action was required.

ATP Safe Sport also continued to drive accountability for online abuse. During the past year, cases were referred to local, national and international law enforcement, prosecutorial and government authorities, reinforcing the ATP's commitment to identifying perpetrators and supporting action beyond content moderation.

The programme's direct support for players continued to grow, with an increasing number of cases being brought to ATP Safe Sport by players and their representatives, enabling tailored safeguarding and investigative support.

Andrew Azzopardi, ATP Director of Safeguarding, said: "Player welfare sits at the heart of the ATP's safeguarding work. Preventing more than 234,000 abusive comments from reaching players and fans demonstrates the tangible impact the programme is having every day. Online abuse has no place in tennis. We will keep investing in the technology, expertise and partnerships that protect players, and we will continue working with the authorities to hold those responsible to account."

Adam Pennock, Sportradar VP of Integrity Services, said: "The scale of abuse identified during the past year underlines why proactive safeguarding measures are essential in modern sport. By combining AI-enabled moderation with specialist investigations, threat assessment and collaboration with authorities, ATP Safe Sport is helping protect players while supporting meaningful action against those responsible for online abuse."

As ATP Safe Sport continues to evolve, the programme will further strengthen player support, expand engagement across the ATP Tour and enhance its safeguarding capabilities through continued innovation and collaboration with its partners.

title: Keys, Townsend, Li Join Gauff on U.S. BJK Cup Squad
article_text:
Grand Slam champions will lead Team USA’s charge in Delray Beach next month.

The 2025 Australian Open champion and world No. 21 Madison Keys, world No. 25 Ann Li, four-time Grand Slam doubles champion and world doubles No. 2 Taylor Townsend and world doubles No. 9 Nicole Melichar-Martinez will join Coco Gauff on the U.S. Billie Jean King Cup Team as it takes on Hungary in a Billie Jean King Cup Playoff November 21-22nd at the Delray Beach Tennis Center.

Today’s announcement comes two weeks after Gauff was named to Team USA.

Two-time Grand Slam champion Gauff will anchor the U.S. Billie Jean King Cup Team at the Delray Beach Tennis Center. It’s a homecoming weekend for Gauff, who grew up in Delray Beach and still often trains in her hometown.

The Hungarian team has nominated world singles No. 75 Ana Bondar, No. 153 Dalma Galfi, No. 445 Amarissa Toth, doubles No. 60 Fanny Stollar and doubles No. 187 Adrienn Nagy.

The best-of-five match series will be played over Saturday and Sunday, with the winner returning to the Qualifying pool and having the chance to compete for the BJK Cup championship in 2027.

Two-day ticket packages are on sale via Ticketmaster.com and are available for $50. Single-day tickets for Saturday or Sunday are on sale for $35. Please visit usta.com/billiejeankingcup for more information.

Matches will start at 1:30 p.m. ET both Saturday and Sunday. Saturday’s schedule will feature two singles matches between each country’s top two nominated players. Sunday’s schedule will feature a doubles match, then two more singles matches to decide the tie. The first nation between the USA and Hungary to win three out of those five matches wins the Playoff, with an amended Sunday schedule possible if either nation clinches victory in the third or fourth match of the weekend. Tennis Channel will carry coverage in the U.S.

Captains may make up to three changes to their nominated rosters by November 20. The U.S. is captained by International Tennis Hall of Famer and U.S. Billie Jean Cup legend Lindsay Davenport, who captained the American side to the BJK Cup final in 2025. Hungary is captained by Kornel Bardoczky.

Gauff, 22, led the U.S. Billie Jean King Cup team to a 4-0 sweep of Austria the last time the U.S. women played in her native Delray Beach, in 2023. Since then, she’s won both the US Open and French Open titles and has gone 47-15 in singles this year, including semifinal appearances at both the US Open and Wimbledon.

Keys, 31, is coming off a year in which she won her 11th career WTA title and went 35-15 in singles. The 2025 Australian Open singles champion has represented the U.S. in Billie Jean King Cup eight times since debuting in 2014. This would mark her competitive debut at the Delray Beach Tennis Center.

Li, 26, is ranked a career-high No. 25 in singles on the heels of beating Aryna Sabalenka to reach the W1000 quarterfinals in Wuhan, China, last week. A Philadelphia-area native, Li won her second career WTA singles title last year on hard courts in Guangzhou before breaking into the Top 30 for the first time this year. This is her debut Billie Jean King Cup nomination.

Townsend, 30, is ranked No. 2 in doubles and has a 39-4 doubles record in 2026. This year she also completed the doubles Career Grand Slam by winning the French Open and US Open. Townsend is 6-2 all-time in Billie Jean King Cup competition since debuting in 2015.

Melichar-Martinez, 33, is ranked No. 9 in doubles and has won two of her 20 career doubles titles in 2026. She represented the U.S. in its Billie Jean King Cup Qualifying competition earlier this year in Belgium and won, partnering with Caty McNally.

title: Springbok Women roll the dice with reshuffled pack for Ireland Test
article_text:
The Springbok Women will face Ireland for the first time in 20 years with a reshuffled front row following injury to captain Babalwa Latsha.

Co-head-coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have moved Xoliswa Khuzwayo to tighthead prop, and named Sanelisiwe Charlie at loosehead prop. Anushka Groenewald retains her spot at hooker.

Replacement loosehead prop Yonela Ngxingolo is in line to earn her 50th cap and will be just the second player to reach that milestone. Lindelwa Gwala and Thandile Mazwi will also offer front-row support from the bench.

Franzel September, Springbok Women co-head coach, said: “We could call on Thandile with great confidence as she played for us already this year and did well, the same as Xoliswa, who has been in the squad all season.

“Tighthead is an important position in any team, even more so in our squad where we rate our scrums as a factor in any match, so having depth there worked out nicely for us.

“As a squad we are also extremely pleased for Yonela and her family and happy that she could share this milestone in front of what we hope to be a good crowd at Athlone Stadium.

“She has been around since 2018 and in recent seasons, she became a very strong bench player for us, something she will do again this weekend.”

Sizophila Solontsi captains the team from the back-row alongside Lerato Makua and Aseza Hele. Catha Jacobs partners Vainah Ubisi in the second row.

In the backs, Unam Tose starts at scrum-half and Byrhandré Dolf is named at fly-half. Maria Tshiremba’s inclusion on the wing is the only other change to the team that beat Spain 20-0 last time out. She starts in a back three with Jakkie Cilliers and Alichia Arries. Shiniqwa Lamprecht and Maceala Samboya are the starting centres.

title: Referees for World Rugby Nations Cup confirmed
article_text:
World Rugby has confirmed the match official appointments for the November leg of the inaugural Nations Cup, with 18 referees from 11 unions set to oversee 18 matches across Europe and Hong Kong between November 6 and 21.

The competition resumes on November 6 following three rounds of action in July, with Georgia and the USA the only unbeaten teams remaining and currently leading their respective pools.

The Nations Cup brings together 12 Rugby World Cup 2027-qualified nations from emerging and developing rugby markets. Alongside the Nations Championship, it forms part of World Rugby’s new global competition structure designed to increase meaningful international fixtures and provide a clearer pathway towards the expanded 24-team Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Australia’s Angus Gardner will referee the opening fixture of the November window when Romania host Tonga in Bucharest on November 6.

New Zealand referee Ben O’Keeffe is set to reach a milestone in Spain’s clash with Uruguay on November 7, taking charge of his 60th Test match.

The tournament will conclude on November 21 when Wales’ Ben Breakspear referees Zimbabwe versus Chile at Stade Chanzy in Angoulême, France. Breakspear is one of five referees who also officiated Nations Cup matches during the July window.

World Rugby said appointments were made with both development and Rugby World Cup preparation in mind, giving officials experience with teams they could oversee at the 2027 tournament while ensuring competing nations benefit from some of the most experienced referees currently on the international panel.

World Rugby also announced appointments for five representative fixtures in October and November.

Georgia’s Nika Amashukeli will referee Japan against Fiji in Tokyo on October 24, a rematch of the recent Pacific Nations Cup final. He will also take charge of England A versus Argentina XV in Bath on November 6.

Japan’s Katsuki Furuse and Argentina’s Damián Schneider will oversee the two USA versus Australia A fixtures, while England’s George Selwood has been appointed to referee Ireland XV against Fiji A in Cork on November 20.

Appointments for the Nations Championship Northern Hemisphere Series are due to be announced separately.

title: François Ratier makes eight changes to France XV after Black Ferns thrashing
article_text:
François Ratier has made eight changes to his starting XV in response to France’s 81-12 drubbing at the hands of the Black Ferns a week ago.

Last week in Hamilton, a young squad selected by the head coach were comprehensively beaten by a rampant New Zealand side. For that fixture, Ratier included several debutants in his team, but has now turned to some of his more experienced players ahead of the second Test in Whang?rei.

This includes the return to the starting team of Émilie Boulard, Gabrielle Vernier and Carla Arbez. Both Ambre Mwayembe and Cloé Correa have returned to the squad after serving their bans.

Anaïs Grando replaces Léa Murie on the wing, while Mathilde Lazarko is installed at hooker ahead of Élisa Riffonneau, who started the last three Tests. Lou Roboam is included as a starter for the first time after making appearances from the bench against Canada and the Black Ferns.

Already in the WXV Global Series, France have lost two Tests against the Black Ferns. A third defeat — or even a fourth next week — would leave a sour mood around this developing French squad until the 2027 Guinness Women’s Six Nations.

France head coach François Ratier said: “Naturally, they would have preferred to kick off their campaign with a win back in France. But instead, they’re making their debut in New Zealand against what is currently the best team in the world.

“New Zealand — well, we’ll see how things evolve over time — but right now, they are the best. It’s simply a matter of making sure everyone is on the same page regarding what just happened, where we currently stand in our cycle, and where we go from here. That’s all there is to it. There aren’t different layers or levels to our discussions with the players.

“The younger ones listen, they learn, and one day they will be in a position to perform against this calibre of team — and they’ll remember that things weren’t always this way.”

title: Wales milestone for Callender as Metcalfe sisters start
article_text:
Flanker Alex Callender will win her 50th cap for Wales in Saturday's WXV Global Series game against Japan - while sisters Nel and Branwen Metcalfe will start their first Test together.

Head coach Sean Lynn has made three personnel changes to the starting line-up from September's narrow defeat by USA at Cardiff Arms Park.

Nel Metcalfe returns from injury on the wing, Seren Lockwood is back at scrum-half and Jorja Aiono gets the nod at lock.

There are two positional changes with Carys Cox switching to centre and Keira Bevan starting at fly-half.

Callender, co-captain with fellow back-row forward Kate Williams, will lead Wales out in Tokyo (10:30 BST) when bringing up her half-century of caps.

Live on iplayer and BBC Sport website & app. Audio commentary on Sounds, BBC Radio Wales Extra & BBC Radio Cymru.

Callender won her first cap in 2019 and hits 50 after returning impressively from injuries suffered before, during and after the 2025 World Cup.

The 26-year-old made a comeback in June's uncapped fixture against the Barbarians, was named as player of the match against South Africa and scored against USA.

"Whenever you talk about a Welsh person everything is about calon and passion - that's her in abundance," said Lynn.

"Whenever she puts that jersey on she wears it with pride and wants to represent the nation. She galvanises this group incredibly, on the pitch and off it."

Callender is a combative flanker but Lynn is quick to point out her deft touches.

"Everybody has always seen Alex as a very passionate individual with phenomenal tackling and breakdown work," said the head coach.

"But she has grown her game and is a really good operator in the line-out and the attack.

"We've been trying to play her as a forward on the edges and she is excelling after working hard on her handling ability over pre-season.

"We're looking to play an expansive game and having a back-row forward who is just like another back brings another dimension."

Bevan returns to pulling the strings from fly-half after an encouraging performance alongside Lockwood was ended when the scrum-half suffered a head injury against South Africa.

The score was already 26-5 when the 19-year-old went off, which prompted the introduction of outside half Lleucu George.

"They were super exciting in the first 30 minutes in South Africa game," said Lynn.

"Keira just wants the ball in her hands, she wants to move the ball and her maturity with the kicking game is developing.

"Her performance against USA as a scrum-half was very good as well but we saw the damage that Seren can do against South Africa, and also in the Barbarians fixture when she stood out."

The Metcalfe sisters played for Wales together for the first time when lock Branwen came off the bench for her first cap against Canada at the 2025 World Cup.

They started the uncapped fixture against the Baa-Baas but join forces in the XV for the first time at Test level against Japan.

Branwen, 20, starts her sixth successive Test and has a new second-row partner in fellow bright prospect Aiono.

Nel, 21, returns on the wing rather than full-back for her first cap since the World Cup after a knee injury that forced her to sit out the Six Nations.

"She was a shining light at the World Cup, which was tough for us," said Lynn.

"Every time that she gets the ball, something will happen. She has got fitter, stronger and faster, and she's excited to go out there on Saturday."

Wales are 11th in World Rugby's rankings, a spot above Japan.

Last month the Sakura Fifteen lost 55-21 to Italy and were beaten twice by Ireland, 31-24 in the WXV Global Series and 43-19 in an extra Test.

"Japan ran Ireland close in the first Test and they are very efficient in what they do, very regimented," said Lynn, who opts for six forwards on his bench.

"They've got a very good maul and we are not going to be taking them lightly at all."

Neumann; N Metcalfe, Cox, Bell, A Williams; Bevan, Lockwood; M Davies, K Jones, Tuipulotu, B Metcalfe, Aiono, K Williams (co-capt), Callender (co-capt), King.

Replacements: Reardon, Pyrs, E Jones, Crabb, G Evans, B Lewis, George, Keight.

title: Britons Burrage and Dudeney progress in Wrexham
article_text:
Jodie Burrage and Alicia Dudeney led the British efforts on day two of the Lexus Wrexham Open, reaching the second round with impressive victories.

They joined compatriot Hannah Klugman in progressing to Thursday's action at the World Tennis Tour W100 event at Wrexham Tennis & Padel Centre.

title: Nielsen Sports SA puts 150 million sports fan data points behind AI platform
article_text:
- Nielsen Sports SA has launched SIYA (Sponsorship Intelligence Yielding Answers), an AI-powered platform that gives users faster access to sports fan insights through natural-language questions.

- SIYA provides access to more than 150 million sports fan data points, helping brands, broadcasters, rights holders and agencies explore South African sports audience behaviour.

- Unlike generative AI tools that may produce inaccurate information, SIYA retrieves statistics from Nielsen Sports SA’s verified research using governed queries and established rules for respondent eligibility and data weighting.

- SIYA enables sports marketers and media organisations to investigate fan behaviour, viewing platforms, beverage preferences, betting habits and sponsor associations, supporting sponsorship evaluation and media planning.

- Nielsen Sports SA plans to expand SIYA with sports consumption and viewership data, sponsorship news, proprietary research and travel and tourism insights, creating a broader picture of sports fans’ behaviour and commercial value.

Nielsen Sports SA has launched SIYA (Sponsorship Intelligence Yielding Answers), an AI-powered platform designed to give brands, broadcasters, rights holders and agencies faster access to sports fan insights without having to commission research or wait for an analyst to interpret the data.

The platform gives users access to more than 150 million sports fan data points through natural-language prompts, allowing them to ask questions about South African sports audiences and receive answers within minutes.

According to Tumelo Selikane, managing director of Nielsen Sports SA, the platform addresses a gap between the amount of sports research available and the time and expertise required to access it.

“The insight already existed, but it was locked behind time and specialists,” he says. “A brand, broadcaster or rights holder with a question about South African sports fans had to commission a study or wait for an analyst to pull it, which could take days.”

SIYA is designed to make that process self-service, allowing users to interrogate Nielsen Sports SA’s existing fan research when they need an answer.

With growing concerns about the reliability of AI-generated information, Nielsen says SIYA does not generate statistics. Instead, it retrieves data from its verified research using governed queries.

“SIYA does not generate numbers; it retrieves them,” says Selikane. “Every figure comes from a governed query against our actual Nielsen Sports SA survey data.”

The platform applies the same rules an analyst would, including ensuring that only respondents who were genuinely asked a particular question are counted and identifying whether figures are weighted or unweighted.

“The AI interprets the question and presents the answer in plain language, but it cannot invent data,” Selikane says. “When a question falls outside what the underlying research supports, SIYA states that rather than guessing.”

The platform is also being developed for multilingual use. Users can ask questions in their own words, with Nielsen building support across South Africa’s official languages in phases.

Selikane says the challenge is not simply translating a question or answer, but ensuring that statistical meaning and caveats remain intact.

“The genuinely hard part is not translating the words; it is making sure a statistic and its caveats survive translation intact,” he says.

Nielsen expects the faster turnaround to change how organisations use research in sponsorship, audience and media decisions.

“When an answer takes days, you only ask the big, pre-planned questions,” says Selikane. “When it takes a minute, you can test an idea in the room, follow a hunch, and check three options before you commit budget.”

Early users have included sponsorship agencies, broadcasters, a global sports league, a major technology platform and brands outside traditional sports marketing, including education and FMCG.

The questions have also extended beyond the size of a particular fan base.

Users have asked about what fans drink, whether they bet, which platforms they watch on and which sponsors they already associate with teams, looking for potential commercial connections.

Some users have gone further, asking SIYA to help shape media strategies rather than simply provide audience insights.

Nielsen developed SIYA internally over the past year, with Selikane saying control over accuracy was a key reason for taking that approach.

“An off-the-shelf assistant is very good at sounding confident, including when it is wrong, which is the opposite of what a research business can put its name to,” he says.

Building the platform internally allows Nielsen to connect the model directly to its verified data, apply its own rules around bases and weighting, and retain control over client and respondent data.

SIYA is not intended to replace Nielsen’s analysts. Users can escalate complex questions to the company’s research specialists, with the platform handling “fast, factual and repeatable” questions while bespoke, strategic and methodological work remains with analysts.

“The aim is not to replace that expertise; it is to free it for the work only a person should do,” says Selikane.

Future developments will add total audience sports consumption and viewership data, giving clients greater visibility of how fans follow, watch and subscribe to sports across different platforms.

For broadcasters and advertisers, this could provide a more detailed picture of where sports audiences consume content and how that behaviour is changing.

Nielsen also plans to add verified sports sponsorship news, deal announcements and other proprietary research to the platform.

Further ahead, SIYA is expected to incorporate travel and tourism data, allowing brands and rights holders to explore how sports fans travel, where they stay and what influences their travel decisions.

“Ultimately, every piece of in-house research we conduct will feed into SIYA, creating a continually growing source of verified data and insight that connects fan attitudes, behaviours, consumption and commercial activity in one place,” Selikane says.

title: ‘Lot more to prove’: Mark Nawaqanitawase opens up on rugby union return
article_text:
Dual-code superstar Mark Nawaqanitawase is returning to rugby union with a point to prove ahead of Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia, following a remarkable stint with NRL powerhouse the Sydney Roosters.

Nawaqanitawase made 11 appearances for the Wallabies and went to the Paris Olympics with the Australia Men’s Sevens side, before officially switching codes and debuting for the Tricolours on September 6, 2024.

Success seemed to follow the former Wallabies flyer in rugby league, both at club land and with representative teams. Nawaqanitawase finished the 2025 NRL campaign as the top try-scorer and earned a spot in the NRL Dally M Team of the Year.

Nawaqanitawase helped Australia secure a three-nil series sweep of England late last year, won a State of Origin series with the NSW Wales Blues, and starred as the Roosters won the NRL Grand Final earlier this month.

Japan Rugby League One powerhouse the Saitama Panasonic Wild Knights announced on February 9 that Nawaqanitawase had signed on. The 26-year-old is firmly focused on that competition, amid speculation about his Test allegiance.

“I’ve had a short time in union, that I still feel like I have a lot more to give, a lot more to prove,” Nawaqanitawase said on The Good, The Bad & The Rugby.

“There’s a Rugby World Cup next year, I’m moving to Japan which is a cool thing. I also love experiences so that’s another big reason, that’s why I’m going to come back because I want to travel as well.

“There’s a whole bunch of things that I feel like I’ve still got time to do. The main one, like I said, I’ve still got a lot to prove.”

Nawaqanitawase first played for the Wallabies in November 2022, and quickly became a key figure within that side. As a Test rookie, ‘Marky Mark’ crossed for two second-half tries in a stunning comeback to beat Wales 39-34 in Cardiff.

Eddie Jones took as Wallabies head coach ahead of the 2023 Rugby World Cup, where Nawaqanitawase continued touched down for two tries in four matches. But the code-hooper hasn’t played for the Wallabies since, having switched to sevens and league.

“Playing for the Wallabies was a massive honour. I grew up watching them and then to be able to do it, it was amazing,” Nawaqanitawase said.

“Obviously it didn’t go quite well in some of the things we did but I’ll never have a regret or not like that part of my journey. I loved every moment of it.

“There’s some great people that I met. Played with obviously boys that I’d grown up playing with here and there as well so I had a great time doing it.”

title: Argentina With the Entire Arsenal back for London Camp
article_text:
Argentina has the entire arsenal back for the upcoming training camp. Felipe Contepomi has named his strongest roster of the year. It includes the return of regular captain Julián Montoya and over a dozen other players who were unavailable for Los Pumas’ in the recent home matches against Australia and South Africa.

The 33-man roster will assemble in London, England from Monday (October 26) to Wednesday (October 28). The three day camp will be preparation for the Nations Championship. Contepomi will confirm his roster for the November Internationals at the completion of the camp.

The Nations Championship will bring to a close international competition for 2026. The end-of-year tour will see Los Pumas facing Ireland, Italy and France and playing in London against a to be confirmed opponent.

Julián Montoya returns to captain Los Pumas. He featured for Argentina in the July Internationals but was not involved in the three aforementioned test matches wherein Los Pumas had home advantage against South Africa and Australia.

There were twenty players missing from the roster. This is visible in who Felipe Contepomi has recalled as it is a very different roster to that which faced the Springboks and Wallabies. Props Thomas Gallo, and Joel Sclavi are in for the first time this year as is second-rower Pedro Rubiolo, flanker Juan Martín González, center Santiago Chocobares and fullback Juan Cruz Mallía.

Felipe Contepomi has not been shy to rotate players. When compared to Michael Cheika or Mario Ledesma regimes, Contepomi’s tenure has seen an expansion in the size of the roster with more players selected across all positions.

An outcome of this has been a number of seasoned players and developing players miss out on the roster for the camp in London. Notably missing forwards include hooker Bautista Bernasconi, tight head prop Pedro Delgado and second-rowers Matías Alemanno and Franco Molina.

Benjamín Grondona had a break-out performance vs South Africa but is also missing as is center Matías Moroni who has 99 caps for his country.
