title: Tsonga & Ascione: The heavyweight partnership behind Lyon’s new ATP 250
article_text:
Jo-Wilfried Tsonga and Thierry Ascione have built a successful partnership in tennis, first on court and now behind the scenes, as they help usher in a new era for the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes in Lyon.

Relocated from Marseille for 2026, the ATP 250 event is taking place at the state-of-the-art LDLC Arena, giving the indoor tournament a fresh home and the pair a new platform for their ambitions. For former World No. 5 Tsonga and tournament director Ascione, it is the latest chapter in a relationship that began when Tsonga turned to his friend and former rival for help extending his playing career.

“When I was No. 8 in the world a few years back, I went to Thierry,” Tsonga recalled to ATPTour.com in Lyon, cracking a smile. “He was already a good friend. We played against each other on the court… I went to his home and told him I wanted to stop playing tennis. He said, ‘Are you crazy? You’re No. 8 in the world. You cannot do that.’

“Finally, he convinced me to continue, and I said, ‘Okay, I will continue, but you come with me.’ He looked at me like this: ‘What do you mean, coming with you?’ I said, ‘Yeah,’ because he was going to be the coach.”

Ascione joined Tsonga in 2013, helping him rediscover his best form before their partnership moved off court following Tsonga’s retirement at Roland Garros in 2022. Together, they grew All In Group and their tennis academy, founded in 2014, into a wider business.

They co-own the All In Country Club in Lyon, where the academy sits just minutes from the LDLC Arena and provides a training base for tournament players including Flavio Cobolli, Taylor Fritz and Stan Wawrinka.

Now, the arena offers a striking new home for the ATP 250 event. With modern facilities, it gives the relocated tournament a fresh identity and a platform to attract top players and passionate French fans.

“I think, for me, I’m proud because we told each other we would do it, with our teams, and we did it,” Tsonga, the 18-time ATP Tour champion, said. “To achieve something like this is never easy. There is always a trap we can fall into, but we did it. So today, it’s a beautiful indoor tournament, one of the biggest in the world. We’re really proud of it.”

As tournament director, Ascione draws on experience from previous ATP events, including the Open Parc in Lyon and the Open 13 Provence in Marseille, as he aims to establish the new event among the leading ATP 250 tournaments.

Early signs are promising, with Cobolli, Fritz and Tommy Paul headlining a strong field as players look to boost their chances of reaching the Nitto ATP Finals. Enthusiastic French fans have also set the tone, turning out in numbers for Sunday's qualifying matches.

“The success for me started on Sunday when I had 5,000 people in the crowd,” Ascione told ATPTour.com when asked about how he measures the success of a tournament. “I think the arena has changed the game for me as a 250. I think it’s great. It's a really good experience.

“It’s been a lot of work, of course, but with the way it started, in terms of results and the player field, it’s amazing. I'm a bit confident because we have an unbelievable draw.”

For Ascione, the tournament is another step in a relationship with Tsonga that has evolved considerably since their playing days. The pair faced each other twice on the ITF World Tour before becoming friends, with Ascione eventually taking on the role of coach when Tsonga was looking for a way to extend his career.

Their partnership was built on trust and a shared understanding of the game, and that foundation has carried into their work as business partners. Today, rather than preparing for matches together, they are helping create an environment in which the world's best players can compete and fans can experience top-level tennis.

“I think we are a good example of how to make it work, with him performing as he did because he was a real champion,” Ascione said of Tsonga, the former No. 5 player in the PIF ATP Rankings. “Now we are continuing the story as we are doing. I think it’s really nice. We are really lucky.”

That shared journey also has a personal dimension. On Sunday, the pair's children were playing together and watching the tennis from the stands, a reminder that the project is about more than the results on court. For Tsonga and Ascione, building a successful tournament also means helping inspire the next generation and making tennis accessible to families and young fans.

“At the end of the day, we do this for them,” Ascione said.

For Tsonga and Ascione, the goal is clear: turn a shared history on court into a lasting success for Lyon, building a tournament that combines world-class tennis with the passion of French fans.

title: Marta Kostyuk issues update on her injury after missing out on WTA Finals place
article_text:
Marta Kostyuk won’t make her WTA Finals debut in 2026.

The Ukrainian star had an outside chance of qualifying at the expense of Karolina Muchova. Kostyuk needed to win the Ningbo Open and the Pan Pacific Open to steal the last WTA Finals spot, but fell at the first hurdle.

She retired from her opening match in Ningbo against Ekaterina Alexandrova after losing the first set. Kostyuk issued an injury update on social media after missing out on WTA Finals qualification.

“The pain in my wrist came back, and as much as I want to keep playing, I know I need to give it more time to recover. Hoping to be back on court soon. Thank you for your support. See you next year, Asia!” said Kostyuk on Instagram.

Give us one bold prediction for the final months of the 2026 tennis season!

Earlier this year, Kostyuk withdrew from the Billie Jean King Cup Finals due to wrist pain, and unfortunately for the 24-year-old, the pain returned in Ningbo. Retiring from her second-round match against Alexandrova, Kostyuk handed Muchova the last WTA Finals qualification spot.

Kostyuk could yet travel to Indian Wells as an alternate, though. Iga Swiatek, who sits above her in the ‘Race,’ won’t play again in 2026; therefore, Kostyuk will be the first name called if any of the eight WTA Finals participants suffer an injury. The 2026 WTA Finals begins on Saturday, November 6.

The Ukrainian star hadn’t reached a Grand Slam semi-final, won a WTA 1000 event, or been ranked in the top 10 before 2026. She has now done all three, having played the best tennis of her career this season.

Kostyuk reached the French Open semi-finals and the Wimbledon semi-finals, narrowly missing out on a maiden Grand Slam final appearance, losing to the eventual champion on both occasions.

She won her first WTA 1000 title in Madrid, defeating Mirra Andreeva in the final. Kostyuk also reached the Cincinnati Open quarter-finals, where she lost to Coco Gauff.

In total, Kostyuk defeated eight top-10 opponents this season, including Andreeva, Jessica Pegula, and Iga Swiatek. There is no doubt that she is now one of the best players in the world and is certainly one to look out for in 2027.

The 24-year-old is likely to return ahead of the Australian Open, which begins on January 11. In 2026, Kostyuk played the Brisbane International before the Australian Open, where she lost to Aryna Sabalenka in the final.

title: By the numbers: Jovic beats Paolini for second time to reach Ningbo quarters

No. 4 seed Iva Jovic rallied from a break down in the opening set to defeat former world No. 4 Jasmine Paolini in straight sets and reach the quarterfinals of the BNB Ningbo Open on Thursday.

Paolini, a two-time Grand Slam finalist, broke early to take a 3-1 lead before Jovic found her rhythm. The American teenager broke twice to win the opening set 6-4.

Jovic moved two breaks ahead at 4-1 in the second set, but Paolini fought back to cut the deficit to 4-3. Jovic held serve before breaking again to close out a 6-4, 6-3 victory in 1 hour, 22 minutes.

title: Wrexham Open: Britons Jodie Burrage and Alicia Dudeney reach second round
article_text:
Jodie Burrage and Alicia Dudeney led the British efforts on day two of the Lexus Wrexham Open, reaching the second round with impressive victories.

They joined compatriot Hannah Klugman in progressing to Thursday's action at the World Tennis Tour W100 event at Wrexham Tennis & Padel Centre.

Burrage beat world-ranked 180 Eva Vedder of the Netherlands 6-2 7-5 in the day's opening encounter to set up a second-round match against Germany's Noma Noha Akugue, the event's fourth seed.

British number seven Dudeney, the world number 232, triumphed 6-4 6-4 against Germany's Tessa Johanna Brockmann and will next face seventh seed Susan Bandecchi of Switzerland.

The Czech Republic's Anna Siskova took a notable scalp by downing Alina Charaeva in three sets.

The Armenian hit the headlines earlier this month by beating world number one Elena Rybakina at the China Open, but Charaeva came unstuck as Siskova hit back from losing the first set to win 4-6 6-3 6-2.

Reigning champion Mimi Xu, from Swansea, is not defending her title this year, instead opting to compete at the W75 Saguenay tournament in Canada.

title: Andreescu, Dabrowski headline Canada's roster for Billie Jean King Cup playoffs
article_text:
TORONTO — Bianca Andreescu, Kayla Cross, Gabriela Dabrowski and Ariana Arseneault will represent Canada at next month’s Billie Jean King Cup playoffs in Brazil.

Tennis Canada announced the four-player roster Wednesday for the Nov. 20-21 tie in Vitoria, Brazil, which will be contested on outdoor clay courts.

Eighth-ranked Canada will face 19th-ranked Brazil in a best-of-five series, with the winner advancing to the 2027 qualifiers.

Andreescu, the 2019 U.S. Open champion, is coming off her biggest tournament victory since 2019 after winning a WTA 125 event in Italy on Sunday.

Dabrowski, ranked fourth in the world in doubles, will make her 21st Billie Jean King Cup appearance and could face her regular doubles partner, Brazil’s Luisa Stefani.

Canada, which won the competition in 2023, has a 12-0 all-time record against Brazil but is coming off a 3-1 loss to Kazakhstan in the qualifiers earlier this year.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 21, 2026.
